newsitem.title: USA: Highlands cuts Vik Brothers purchase price.
newsitem.headline: Highlands cuts Vik Brothers purchase price.

text.p: HIghlands Insurance Group Inc Friday said it reached an agreement in principle to reduce the purchase price of Vik Brothers Insurance to $110 million from the $164 million value originally agreed upon in June 1996.
Under the revised terms of the acquisition of Lawrenceville, N.J.,-based Vik, HIghlands said its contingent payments of up to $32 million based on Vik's future results have been eliminated.

The firm said the revised terms reflect a net loss of $8.9 million for Vik for the nine months ended September 30, 1996. This loss is primarily the result of significant catastrophe losses in excess of $17 million incurred by Vik in July and September.
In addition, the revised terms reflect the recent announcement by A.M. Best Company that its rating of VBII was being reduced from "B+" (very good) to "B-" (adequate).

Upon the signing of the amendment, Highlands, rated "A-" (excellent) by A.M. Best, will enter into an agreement with Vik to reinsure all of Vik's new and renewal business written from January 1, 1997 to the date the acquisition is completed. If the acquisition is not completed, this reinsurance agreement will be terminated.

Highlands said it will finance the acquisition with a combination of preferred stock (or similar securities), common stock and bank debt. Highlands will issue approximately 1.2 million shares of common stock, representing approximately 9.4 percent of Highlands' then outstanding common equity.
Following completion of the acquisition, Highlands intends to contribute up to a maximum of $42 million of capital to the Vik's insurance subsidiaries.
